name: Cecil Street Garden
address: Kingsessing Avenue & Cecil Street, Philadelphia, PA 19143
description: A community garden on a reclaimed Kingsessing corner lot, listed in the Park in a Truck toolkit as "Cecil Street Park" and used as a planting-prototype site with LandHealth Nursery. It's since become part of a federally funded pollinator-habitat network linking several Southwest Philadelphia Park in a Truck sites, planted with native trees and echinacea. Resident Victoria Miles-Chambliss: "Our block has really changed since we put in the garden. It's like an oasis in the middle of Southwest Philadelphia."

name: Melon Street Park
description: Park in a Truck's first-ever park, opened October 2019 on a vacant Mantua lot (about 2,400 sq ft). Mantua Civic Association president DeWayne Drummond: "The ground that we're standing on right now, it was a vacant lot. Now, it's beautified by community members and the youth." Founder Kim Douglas describes it as a park that "can drain stormwater, grow plants, provide habitat for wildlife, and host entertainment."

name: Glenda Anne Memorial Park
description: Dedicated August 3, 2019 on a formerly-dumped-on lot, with 200+ neighbors and elected officials attending; Glenda Ann Christopher's family accepted the park as her memorial (press coverage spells it "Glenda Ann Christopher Memorial Park"). A pollinator garden was added in spring 2023 — organizer Greg Thompson: "A week or two after it went in they were there — bees, birds, butterflies and a lot more insects than we've ever seen." A second dedication in June 2024 celebrated that addition; youth volunteer Semaj Flores: "We got involved in this for the environment and for the youth to help younger kids that's dealing with gun violence."

name: S 60th St & Greenway Ave

description: A Park in a Truck site a block from Glenda Anne Memorial Park, in the same Kingsessing greening corridor — listed in the toolkit's acknowledgments (credited to Ted Behr, Southwest Globe Times) as a separate line from Glenda Anne. name: Tilden Middle School
description: Students built a pollinator/habitat garden at Tilden Middle School as part of the same Southwest Philadelphia pollinator network that includes Cecil Street Garden, funded in part by Pew Charitable Trusts through Audubon Mid-Atlantic with Park in a Truck as a partner. Youth are paid through PiaT's Park Ambassador program to maintain it and monitor pollinators.

name: Streetscape of Brewerytown Garden
description: Listed on Park in a Truck's own site directory, near Dover Street Pocket Park in Brewerytown. This is a different project from Neighborhood Gardens Trust's unrelated "Brewerytown Garden" at 27th & Master St. No independent news coverage was found — details beyond the approximate location are not yet confirmed.
